correctness.rationale: For all N>=1, r>d>0, p_i>0 and initial 0<T<=1, P=sum p_i x_i x_{i+1}<=p_*T^2, hence logistic comparison yields uniform T>=min(T0,(r-d)/(r+p_*)). If m=min initially occupied site then u_i=x_i/x_m are decreasing, x_m/T bounded below, and clock tau=int_0^t x_m ds >= delta t. The triangular exact system du_i/dtau=-p_{i-1}u_{i-1}u_i determines by induction whether u_i has positive limit (preceding absent/decays) or decays exponentially (preceding positive), giving the greedy support with no dependence on magnitude of positive p_i. P(t) decays, logistic relaxation gives T->K=1-d/r exponentially, and each x_i tends exponentially to the claimed equilibrium. For N=3 integrate u_2 in tau to obtain R and exact limiting abundances. Independently solved N=3 IVP and matched exact limit to 1.4e-12; not a proof. No convergence statement when demographic rates differ or p_i=0.

originality.rationale: PASS (best of knowledge): Samanta et al study the same hierarchical directed model and establish only independent-set equilibrium restrictions and transverse/numerical observations; a stable independent set is not the trajectory-selected greedy independent set. The exact triangular time-change proves global convergence from every nonzero nonnegative initial state, initial-support selection, exponential rate, and abundance split. Baigent–Ching attract a continuum and Hou assumes a unique common attractor; neither implies the history-dependent all-N result. Standard competitive triangular techniques may overlap in older unindexed literature, recorded as risk.
residual_risks: Only homogeneous r,d with strictly positive directed p_i and initial 0<T<=1; heterogeneous rates and absent-species immigration are excluded.

value.rationale: PASS: The source paper identifies coexistence-compatible independent sets without deciding which one a trajectory reaches. A global all-N greedy support rule and exact surviving abundances solve a meaningful selection problem for the specified deterministic ecological chain, including arbitrary positive predation rates and boundary initial supports. The rate of convergence is not uniform over initial states.
